No stickers caught yet.\n\nWhen an iPhone sticker arrives it shows up here. You can also open a file from the menu, or share a picture to LightDecoder from another app.

LightDecoder can pick up stickers from your message notifications and decode them here, so you don\'t have to share each one.\n\nThis needs notification access, which you turn on in Android\'s settings. Notification access lets an app see all your notifications. LightDecoder only uses the ones from Google Messages and Samsung Messages, keeps what it catches on this phone, and sends nothing anywhere.
HEIC stickers and pictures from Messages show up here by themselves. Pictures that Messages can already show are left alone.

If the switch is greyed out

Android blocks this switch for apps installed from a file until you allow it.

1. Tap the greyed-out switch once, so Android shows its warning.
2. Tap "Open app info" below.
3. Tap the ⋮ menu in the top corner and choose "Allow restricted settings".
4. Come back here and tap "Turn on" again.
Delete this sticker from the inbox?
Delete every sticker in the inbox? Stickers you saved to your gallery are kept.
Keep every picture, not only HEIC

LightDecoder opens HEIC stickers and pictures with its own built-in decoder (libheif and libde265, LGPL-3.0), so it does not depend on what the phone supports.

The Google Messages link uses libgm from mautrix-gmessages (AGPL-3.0, github.com/mautrix/gmessages) and other open-source Go modules (MIT, BSD-3-Clause, MPL-2.0).

What LightDecoder keeps stays on this phone. It has no servers and no analytics; the Google Messages link, if you set it up, talks only to Google.

Source code: github.com/ClockworkBlack/LightDecoder (AGPL-3.0)

Enter the code shown by the relay app on your iPhone. LightDecoder then verifies this phone\'s number with Apple by one text message, as an iPhone does.
Enter the relay code from the relay app on your iPhone.

Apple verifies the number by a text message: LightDecoder sends one to Apple\'s gateway for your carrier and reads Apple\'s reply. Your carrier may charge for that one text. Android will ask to let LightDecoder send and receive SMS.
Registering a phone number needs permission to send and receive SMS.
Apple answers the verification text with one that starts with REG-RESP. If it shows up in your messages app and LightDecoder did not pick it up, copy all of it and paste it here.
Nothing is waiting for Apple\'s reply right now. Tap Register first.
That is not Apple\'s reply: it should start with REG-RESP and contain r=, n= and s=.
That reply is for an earlier attempt (its r= number differs). Use the reply to the latest verification text.

Once iMessage is on, iMessage conversations are in the Messages tab with your texts, and LightDecoder stays connected in the background so they arrive whether it is open or not. A new conversation with someone who has iMessage starts as an iMessage.
Reactions can\'t be sent over iMessage from LightDecoder yet.
